correctness.rationale: Every vertex of a 3-periodic GHM trajectory is either always zero or advances through 0,1,2 once; a connected graph cannot mix both types because a cycling neighbor would excite a stationary zero. Hence nonfixed 3-periodic colorings are exactly those where every i has a successor-colored neighbor at offsets ±1,±2. The 81-state length-four-word transfer T tests the central vertex, and closed walks of length n biject to labelled period-three states for n>=5. An independently built exact integer 81×81 matrix has characteristic polynomial X^69(X+1)(X³−3X²+2X−2)(X⁴+X³+2X²+3X+4)^2; Newton/trace identity yields the all-n formula. Independent direct GHM simulations gave P5..P8=150,270,588,1548. The cubic has unique root rho≈2.52138 and other roots modulus sqrt(2/rho)<1; scaled Eneström–Kakeya bounds quartic roots by 2, so P_n=rho^n+O(2^n). For nearest-neighbor cycles every directed successor edge must be used, forcing cyclic ±1 color increments and six states iff 3|n. Exact polynomial matrix identity is a finite certificate proving all n jointly with the transfer bijection, not an extrapolated enumeration.
